readings: rst is an asynchronous level-sensitive reset: c is forced to 0 whenever rst is high (and the first clock edge after rst goes low accumulates a*b)

rst is edge-triggered as written ("positive edge of the reset signal"): c is cleared only on the rising edge of rst, so while rst stays high across several clock edges c keeps its previous value and no accumulation occurs, while a clock edge occurring after the single rising edge is ignored
a and b are signed 32-bit integers: a*b is a signed 64-bit product accumulated into a signed accumulator (e.g. a=-1, b=1 clears the accumulator)
a and b are unsigned 32-bit integers: a*b is an unsigned 64-bit product accumulated into an unsigned accumulator (e.g. 32'hFFFFFFFF * 1 adds 4294967295)

ambiguities.aspect: Accumulator width / overflow and truncation point
readings: The 64-bit product is added to a full-precision internal accumulator and only the low 32 bits are presented on c, so overflow beyond 32 bits is retained internally and reappears later
The product is truncated to 32 bits (or the accumulator is 32 bits) and addition wraps mod 2^32, so overflow is discarded immediately
Overflow saturates at 32'h7FFFFFFF / 32'hFFFFFFFF instead of wrapping
c is a pure register: it holds the accumulation up to (but excluding) the current cycle's product, i.e. the product sampled at clock edge N appears on c during cycle N+1
c is registered but updated such that the product applied at the same clock edge is visible on c in the same cycle (combinational bypass of the newest product)
